setting.text: We use X to denote an arbitrary countable universe of strings; typically X = Σ∗. We fix an arbitrary canonical ordering of the domain X and denote it by (x_1, x_2, . . .). A language is an infinite subset L ⊆ X.
If G always outputs singletons, we say it is an element-based generator. If G outputs infinite sets, we say it is a set-based generator.

The algorithm G is said to generate from K in the limit if, for all enumerations of K, there is some n∗ ∈ N such that for all steps n ≥ n∗,
1. if G is element-based, then G_n(H_n) ∈ K \ S_n;
2. if G is set-based, then G_n(H_n) ⊆ K \ S_n.
The collection L allows for generation in the limit (or is generable) if there is an algorithm G that generates from K in the limit for any K ∈ L.

quotes.text: A collection L is generable in the limit with mistake feedback by an element-based generator (Definition 3) if and only if L has a countable inner-cover (Definition 4).

terms.text:
A collection L has a countable inner-cover if there exists a countable family C = {C_1, C_2, . . .} of subsets of X such that:
1. |C_i| = ∞ for every i ∈ N, and

2. for every L ∈ L there exists i ∈ N with C_i ⊆ L.
In this case, we call C a countable inner-cover of L.

quotes.text: A collection L is generable in the limit with mistake feedback by a set-based generator if and only if L is generable in the limit with mistake feedback by an element-based generator.

quotes.text:
The following statements hold for collections L in the no-feedback model.
1. If L has an inner-cover of finite size, then L is generable in the limit.
2. If L is generable in the limit, then L has a countable inner-cover (Definition 4).
Further, the following hold:
1. There is a collection L with a countable inner-cover that is not generable in the limit.
2. There is also a collection L that is generable in the limit and has a countable inner-cover.
3. There is also a collection L that is generable in the limit and does not have a finite inner-cover.

terms.text: Informally, a collection C is an inner-cover of another collection L if for every language L ∈ L there exists some C ∈ C with C ⊆ L and |C| = ∞; see Definition 4.

In this case, we call C a countable inner-cover of L.
